Results

The pooled mean difference for multiple trial-declared outcomes: Modified Neuropathy Impairment Score +7 (mNIS+7) | Change From Baseline in the Modified Neurologic Impairment Score +7 (mNIS+7) at Month 9 Between the Vutrisiran Group (HE | Change From Baseline in Modified Neuropathy Impairment Score Plus 7 (mNIS+7) at Week 66 was -25.1 (-34.9 to -15.3) across 3 trials, against not recorded on the page this object was extracted from.1

THIS POOL IS REFERRED, NOT WITHDRAWN. UNIT OF ANALYSIS -- the three rows are not the same kind of comparison. APOLLO contributes patisiran against its OWN randomised placebo. HELIOS-A contributes vutrisiran against APOLLO's placebo, an EXTERNAL control. NEURO-TTRansform contributes eplontersen against NEURO-TTR's placebo, a second external control -- and its arms are recorded on this object with inotersen as the treatment, which the registration contradicts. TWO OF THREE POOLED VALUES ARE NON-RANDOMISED EXTERNAL-CONTROL COMPARISONS RECORDED AS RANDOMISED ARM CONTRASTS, and PATISIRAN IS THE INTERVENTION IN ONE ROW AND THE COMPARATOR IN ANOTHER inside a single pooled number. Withdrawing a published estimate is a published-number decision and belongs to Mahmood. The finding is complete and stated; the estimate is unchanged. THIS POOL IS REFERRED. THE SAME 77 PATIENTS CONTROL TWO OF THESE THREE CONTRASTS. HELIOS-A has no placebo arm; its registered primary outcome names, in its own words, "the External Placebo Comparator Group [APOLLO (NCT01960348)]". APOLLO's placebo group is 77 patients as posted. So APOLLO's placebo controls both the APOLLO row and the HELIOS-A row, and k = 3 counts two independent control arms as three. THIS IS THE ONE-TRIAL-COUNTED-SEVERAL-TIMES DEFECT THIS PROJECT DOCUMENTS IN PUBLISHED SYNTHESES, in our own pool.2

NOTED ON THIS POOL. A PUBLISHED SYNTHESIS OF THIS QUESTION INCLUDED 10 TRIALS WHERE THIS POOL CARRIES 3. It is NOT a claim that 7 specific trials were missed, and nobody here has identified them. The estimate above is computed from the trials this object carries and is not withdrawn or altered by this note. What a reader is owed is the SCOPE: a larger evidence base on this question exists in the literature, and whether this review's search should be widened is a decision that has not been made. SEPARATELY, this pool is already REFERRED on an obstacle in the evidence: a published feasibility assessment found a network meta-analysis of these treatments NOT FEASIBLE on cross-trial heterogeneity.3

The trials' results were poorly consistent with one another: I-squared, the share of the variation between them that is more than chance alone would produce, was 88.1%; the estimated variance of the true effects between trials (tau-squared) was 65.4, the heterogeneity test statistic Q was 18.3, on degrees of freedom 2. not recorded on the page this object was extracted from4

The grounds for pooling are recorded as: The extractor recovered a pooled result from this page, so the page pooled these trials. Whether they SHOULD have been pooled is not established by conversion - several pages in this corpus pooled harm with efficacy, or distinct agents, and their estimates were withdrawn for that reason. Where a later pool on this page rests on the same grounds, they are not restated.5

The full model output for every pooled outcome -- the call, the estimator, the heterogeneity statistics and the back-transformed interval -- is reproduced verbatim as Extended data at the end of this article, so every number above can be checked against the software that produced it.6

Discussion

DRAFT FOR THE AUTHOR TO REPLACE -- Whether the effect size is clinically meaningful. The pooled MD is -25.11 (95% CI -34.87 to -15.35) over 3 trials. Every contributing interval excludes no effect. WHETHER A CHANGE OF THAT MAGNITUDE IS CLINICALLY MEANINGFUL IN THIS POPULATION IS THE AUTHOR'S JUDGEMENT: NO FIELD ON THIS OBJECT RECORDS A THRESHOLD OF IMPORTANCE, AND NONE IS ASSUMED HERE.1

DRAFT FOR THE AUTHOR TO REPLACE -- Whether the observed heterogeneity is clinically important. Across 3 trials, tau-squared 65.4032; every trial interval excludes no effect. WHETHER THAT DEGREE OF DISAGREEMENT MATTERS CLINICALLY -- WHETHER THE TRIALS ARE ANSWERING THE SAME QUESTION IN THE SAME PATIENTS -- IS THE AUTHOR'S JUDGEMENT.2

DRAFT FOR THE AUTHOR TO REPLACE -- WHY this result differs from the published ones, mechanically or methodologically. This review pools -25.11 (95% CI -34.87 to -15.35) over 3 trials. The appraised synthesis pooled NONE -- the network was assessed and NOT performed. Which trials that synthesis carries: APOLLO is keyed to NCT01960348 on this object and is NAMED in the appraised feasibility assessment, so the overlap is read rather than inferred. The other two trials on this object -- HELIOS-A NCT03759379 and NEURO-TTRansform NCT04136184 -- are NOT in that assessment's trial set, which predates them. WHY THE TWO RESULTS DIFFER -- WHETHER BY POPULATION, OUTCOME DEFINITION, MODEL OR INCLUDED SET -- IS THE AUTHOR'S JUDGEMENT.3

DRAFT FOR THE AUTHOR TO REPLACE -- Whether the evidence base is adequate to answer the question. The evidence base is 3 trials, with no risk-of-bias assessment recorded. WHETHER THAT IS ENOUGH TO ANSWER THE QUESTION DEPENDS ON THE DECISION THE ANSWER IS FOR, WHICH IS NOT STATED ON THIS OBJECT, AND IS THE AUTHOR'S JUDGEMENT.4

Comparison with published syntheses

Published syntheses were identified as follows. PubMed E-utilities, executed 2026-08-20. Query, counts and per-record disposition in ssot/attr-pn-review/appraisal/PUBLISHED_SYNTHESIS_SCREEN.json. 21 records matched, 21 summaries read, 2 appraised against their abstracts, 19 NOT APPRAISED. No included-study table was read for either.1

This review was compared against 2 published synthesis(es); the denominator is stated because a comparison against an unstated number of reviews is not a comparison.2

What this comparison found. THE COMPARISON IS HELD; THE POOL IS REFERRED ON AN OBSTACLE IN THE EVIDENCE. Samjoo et al. 2020 set out to network-meta-analyse ATTR-PN treatments, assessed feasibility, and concluded that 'An NMA of ATTR-PN treatments was not feasible, given the observed cross-trial heterogeneity' -- naming that 'neuropathy outcomes were not evaluated consistently between trials'. THIS OBJECT POOLS mNIS+7, A NEUROPATHY OUTCOME, ACROSS THREE DIFFERENT DRUGS TO -25.11. The obstacle is a property of how the trials were designed and reported, so NOTHING FURTHER WE READ RESOLVES IT: this is an evidence-shaped referral and a finished state, not a gap awaiting more reading. Whether to withdraw the estimate is a content decision and is not made here.3

On what basis their trial set is known: APOLLO is keyed to NCT01960348 on this object and is NAMED in the appraised feasibility assessment, so the overlap is read rather than inferred. The other two trials on this object -- HELIOS-A NCT03759379 and NEURO-TTRansform NCT04136184 -- are NOT in that assessment's trial set, which predates them.4
